plan.english: Of-Good-Horses, my stallion is sweating and does not stand. Did you drive him hard on the road? I drove him for a whole day to the king's village. He is weary, and his heart trembles. Lead him into the shade, and rub his body with grass. Will he carry me in the morning? Let him rest for two days. I will not drive him; you know horses well.

plan.english: Wise one, my wife is standing; what do I owe you? You owe me nothing. But give a calf to Perkwunos. I will give him a calf, and to you I will give wool. I will take the wool. Your house is dear to the storm god. You are a giver of good things.

plan.english: Sister-in-law, the child weeps, and sleep does not come to it. Is it hungry, or is it thirsty? It has sucked; it is not hungry. Then sing it a song. Which song? I know no song. Sing this: little one, may sleep come to you; your mother guards you. Now it is sleeping; your song is sweet.

plan.english: Man-Minded, why are you lying in the field? The sun was heating me while I ploughed, and I grew faint. Go into the shade of the tree, and sip this cold mead. My head is heavy, and my eyes are dark. Lie in the shade; I will plough the field. Woman, you are strong. Today I am stronger than the sun!

plan.english: Old man, teach me the words that join limbs. Why do you want them? My brother's leg is broken, and there is no one in our village who knows them. Listen: sinew with sinew I join, skin with skin I bind. Shall I sing it, or say it? Sing it; my grandmother sang it to me. I will not forget it.

Did he ask for anything? He asked for porridge and for his dog. That is good. Sit with me by the fire until dawn, old woman.

plan.english: Kindly, my back hurts; I carried heavy loads for the whole day. Lie on your belly; I will rub your back with warm butter. Your hands are strong. Do not lift loads in this month. But who will carry them? My brother is small. Your brother will lift them; a young back grows strong. I will tell him, Kindly.

I will carry you home on my back. You are strong, but I am heavy. A friend is not a heavy load. Then carry me, and I will sing your great fame.
